title: The Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire) - Objectives, Development and Status
summary: Pre-flight (May 2016) paper on the three Saffire units: objectives (growth of a large fire in low gravity; low-g flammability vs NASA-STD-6001 Test 1), identical flow-duct hardware (module about 53 x 90 x 133 cm), diagnostics (2 cameras, 4 radiometers, embedded and plume thermocouples, O2/CO2/pressure sensors, 2 anemometers, smoke wire), planned flows (Saffire-I 20 cm/s, Saffire-III 30 cm/s), the Saffire-II sample table, safety design (four latching relays for the igniter) and planned launch/operation dates.

items.claim: Objectives: rate of growth of a large fire in low gravity, and low-g flammability vs the 1-g screening test.
items.quote: The objectives of these experiments are to (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.

items.claim: As planned, Saffire-I was to burn a ~0.94 x 0.4 m fabric at 20 cm/s a few hours after unberthing on 2 June 2016; as flown, the burn used a 94 x 40.6 cm sheet at about 20 cm/s on 14 June 2016, so the flight matched the plan except for the date.
items.quote: Saffire-I will be conducted at an air flow velocity of 20 cm/s while Saffire-III will be run at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s

items.claim: Planned operation date for Saffire-I (2 June 2016), 12 days before the actual burn.
items.quote: As of the writing of this paper, the un- berthing of the Cygnus is scheduled for June 2, 2016 and Saffire-I is scheduled to operate a few hours afterwards.

items.claim: Prior microgravity flame-spread samples were no larger than 10 cm.
items.quote: Prior experiments have been limited to samples no larger than 10 cm in length and width whereas a serious spacecraft fire would likely be much larger and consume much more material.

notes: Held file 'PSI-98_Science Documents_SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status.pdf' (evidence.parquet). The record already used it for question, apparatus, measurements and limitations but not in findings; a method finding (findings[11]) now cites it for the planned-vs-flown conditions. Pre-flight paper: no results.

title: Buoyant Effects on the Flammability of Silicone Samples Planned for the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire)
summary: ICES-2015 ground (1 g) study of the silicone sheets planned for Saffire-II (0.25, 0.36, 0.61, 1.00 mm; 5 x 30 cm Test 1 geometry): upward burn length fell with thickness and the thickest would not ignite; the two thinnest burned completely downward, unusually more flammable than upward; a deposited silica layer is blamed for upward self-extinction; with 2 m/s forced upward flow all ignited thicknesses burned completely.
notes: Ground tests of the Saffire-II silicone samples; nothing about Saffire-I.

title: Flame spread: Effects of microgravity and scale
summary: Combustion and Flame 2019 overview of Saffire-I to -III: 94 x 40.6 cm SIBAL fabric (Saffire-I, III) and nine 29 x 5 cm samples (Saffire-II), forced flow 20-25 cm/s in Cygnus. Concurrent spread over thin fabric reached a steady rate and limiting length; thick PMMA approached a non-growing steady state with a limiting pyrolysis length within 15 min; upward 1-g spread accelerates.

items.claim: Concurrent spread over thin fabric reaches a steady rate and limiting length.
items.quote: The downloaded test data show that a concurrent (downstream) spreading flame over thin fabrics in microgravity reaches a steady spread rate and a limiting length.

notes: Abstract via Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex; Elsevier full text paywalled (no NTRS or PMC copy found).

title: Transient flame growth and spread processes over a large solid fabric in concurrent low-speed flows in microgravity – Model versus experiment
summary: Proc. Combust. Inst. 37 (2019) model-vs-experiment study of concurrent spread over SIBAL fabric at 20 cm/s for the 41 x 94 cm Saffire-I sheet and the 5 x 29 cm Saffire-II strip. Both reached quasi-steady flame length; the large sample's pyrolysis length overshot first (explained by flow reduction in the growing boundary layer); the narrow strip spread about 13% faster with shorter burnout because of better lateral oxygen transport.

items.claim: Large sample: pyrolysis-length overshoot explained by boundary-layer flow reduction; 5 cm strip ~13% faster.
items.quote: While steady state pyrolysis lengths were similar, the 5 cm wide sample had a slightly larger spread rate (by ∼13%) and a shorter burnout time (pyrolysis length over spread rate) compared to the 41 cm wide sample.

notes: Abstract via OpenAlex; full text paywalled.

title: Fire safety in space – beyond flammability testing of small samples
summary: Not read. Acta Astronautica 2015 review by the Fire Safety in Space topical team on the case for large-scale spacecraft fire tests (the rationale for Saffire), written before the flights.
notes: The open HAL copy (hal-01524495) returned an anti-bot challenge page to automated requests; no abstract in Crossref, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar. Pre-flight, so no Saffire results.

title: Operation and Development Status of the Spacecraft Fire Experiments (Saffire)
summary: ICES-2016 paper (written May 2016, before the first burn): Saffire objectives, hardware and samples (0.4 x 0.94 m fabric; nine 5 x 29 cm Saffire-II samples chosen near their MOC at 21% O2), Saffire-I integration and launch on OA-6 (22 March 2016), operations plan, and the Saffire-IV to -VI gap list. No results.

items.claim: Rationale: earlier samples no larger than 10 cm.
items.quote: Prior experiments have been limited to samples no larger than 10 cm in length and width whereas a serious spacecraft fire could consume as much as an order of magnitude more material.

notes: Pre-flight; the PSI-100 publication list gives its NTRS link (20170000230) in the authors field.
